name: Goodricke

guards.text: Ignore the repo's many untracked scratch scripts (backend/scripts/_*, scripts/demo/_*, root-level scratch files) unless the diff itself adds them as part of the change.

guards: Any database check is dev only; never prod (never source a prod .env).

NEVER change the checkout of /home/carls/apps/mike-dev: no git checkout, switch, stash, reset, restore, clean, merge, rebase or bisect, not even `checkout --detach`. Other sessions and the running dev stack use that working tree; changing it breaks them.

guards.text: For a git range, the files on disk are NOT the reviewed version (/home/carls/apps/mike-dev is a shared checkout on another branch).
Weigh client-visible wording, ethical walls, de-id and audit invariants heavily.

Return every changed file (excluding untracked scratch) with a kind judged from its path: frontend/src/app and frontend/src/components = ui; backend/migrations = migration; *.test.ts / *.spec.* / test dirs = test; docs/, *.md = docs; other backend/src = backend; anything else = other.
touchesSecurity: any change under backend/src/lib/docreview*, auth / mcpAuth / middleware, deid / deident, permissions / accessControl / access.ts, ethicalWalls, audit.

touchesClientWording: any change to code or text that renders client-visible wording — reports (docreviewReport*, report stores), engagement letters/packs (engagement*), LLM prompts or rubrics, document templates.
Ignore the repo's many untracked scratch scripts (backend/scripts/_*.ts etc.).
The dev stack serves this checkout live: never run npm run dev, restart services or delete .next.
Database work is dev only; never prod.
Flag PostgREST list reads without a .range() paging loop.

reviewFinders.brief: the Goodricke invariants: ethical walls enforced on every document/matter read; Principal / canAct checks on every mutating route; audit rows written exactly once per action (never zero, never twice on retry); PII and client identities never logged or sent unmasked past the de-id gateway; PostgREST silently caps .select() at 1000 rows, so any list read that can grow needs a .range() paging loop; supabase-js stays pinned at exact 2.102.1.

behaviour the change breaks for existing callers, removed or weakened tests, new behaviour with no test, tests that assert rule text rather than measured outcomes, a page root that lost h-full + overflow-y-auto, a behavioural change with no CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entry.

signOff.implementer: CHANGELOG: if app behaviour changed, the CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entry is part of the deliverable — add exactly ONE bullet line in the house form `- **Added|Changed|Fixed|Removed — <summary>.** <detail>` (the Keep a Changelog group is the bullet's prefix; read a few existing entries first), British English, no exclamation marks, describing the change itself (never test counts). Put it under this work's `### <Area — topic>` heading if one already exists near the top of [Unreleased], else directly below `## [Unreleased]`; never add headings. It is the one shared file: re-read it immediately before editing, insert only your line, never rewrite other lines; if the edit fails because the file changed, re-read and retry. Pure refactors/tests/docs need no line (return "").
signOff.reviewer: a missing or wrong CHANGELOG line for a behaviour change
signOff.seat: Before committing, check CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] has the line of each listed piece that changed app behaviour, and commit each line in the same commit as its piece's code.

signOff.trigger: any change to a page root (a frontend/src/app page or layout, or a component that becomes a page root)
signOff.implementer: If you change a page root (a frontend/src/app page/layout, or a component that becomes a page root), say so in notes and list scroll-audit in triggered so the seat runs the scroll audit; page roots use h-full + overflow-y-auto.
signOff.seat: Before sign-off, run the scroll audit against the running dev stack on the pages the listed pieces touch, with enough data to overflow, and put its verdict in the sign-off: `cd scripts/demo && LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$HOME/.local/chrome-libs/extract/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu node _scroll-audit.mjs [/your/new/page ...]` (a FITS verdict only means the seeded data was short).
